claims.text: Tdap: 1 dose each preg, whatever the prior Hx
claims.quote: Pregnant patients should receive 1 dose of Tdap during each pregnancy, irrespective of their history of receiving the vaccine.

claims.text: Tdap @ 27–36 wks, preferably early in that window
claims.quote: Tdap should be administered at 27 to 36 weeks gestation, preferably during the earlier part of this period, although it may be administered at any time during pregnancy (4).

claims.text: Inactivated flu vaccine (IIV3): all ≥6 mo, incl preg
claims.quote: Inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) can be administered to all people ≥ 6 months, including pregnant patients.

claims.text: Live intranasal flu vaccine (LAIV3): only if ⍉preg
claims.quote: Live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV3) (intranasal influenza vaccine) can be administered to healthy people aged 2 to 49 years who are not pregnant and who do not have immunocompromising conditions.

claims.text: RSV (Abrysvo): preg @ 32–36 wks, protects infants to 6 mo
claims.quote: ABRYSVO is a vaccine indicated for active immunization of pregnant individuals at 32 through 36 weeks gestational age for the prevention of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and severe LRTD caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants from birth through 6 months of age.
claims.locator: ABRYSVO (respiratory syncytial virus vaccine) prescribing information

claims.text: MMR: ⍉immune → vaccinate when preg is completed, before discharge
claims.quote: Pregnant patients who do not have evidence of immunity should be vaccinated when pregnancy is completed and before they are discharged from the health care facility.
claims.locator: MSD › Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) Vaccine
